text:
fran: New contributor flagged the onboarding sample spamming DEBUG when OTEL is on. Also saw missing req_id on a couple of retry lines and an email in a header leak.

ty: Can you paste the exact steps + a tiny log clip?

fran: Steps: `git checkout samples/onboard && npm ci && TELEMETRY=enabled REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=debug ./dev up`. Clip: 
```
2026-07-12T07:22:01.100Z INFO startup service ready
2026-07-12T07:22:01.241Z DEBUG undici sending request POST /v1/respond
2026-07-12T07:22:01.242Z DEBUG undici raw-headers: Authorization: Bearer sk-... user_email=zoe@example.com
2026-07-12T07:22:01.243Z DEBUG retry attempt=1 missing req_id in context
```
fran: The token is redacted but `user_email` is visible. When I switch `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=otel_first` the number of lines lacking req_id increases.

ty: Which SDK is the sample pinned to? We moved the injection earlier in 0.9.x and added an ensureReqId helper. Older pins can emit logs before injection.

fran: package.json has "redwood-sdk": "0.8.11". I tried local upgrade to 0.9.3 and the problem mitigates but not fully: one internal debug line from undici still leaked the header.

ty: Two things then: (A) bump sample SDK to >=0.9.3 so injection/backfill exists, (B) add a tiny, defensive header-normalization in our lowest-level HTTP primitive that runs before any call into undici/fetch and scrubs email/token/ip patterns. That should catch internal debug paths.

fran: I worry about double-redact: some code already redacts Authorization; if we naively replace tokens we may get `Bearer <redacted_token>` turning into `Bearer <redacted_token>` twice.

ty: Good point. Implementation should idempotently replace only if pattern matches raw email/token, not if value already contains `<redacted_`. Add unit tests for double-redact cases.

fran: Also retry logs often print before wrappers. Can we ensure req_id is stamped into the request context before retry logging runs?

ty: Yes — the SDK's `ensureReqId()` should be called at the top of retry middleware. For older sample pins, include a local shim that calls it early. We'll also add a best-effort backfill that marks logs with `req_id=unknown` instead of empty when unavailable.

ci-bot: CI suggestion: add integration job `onboard/logs-scan` that runs sample with `TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER=otel_first` and greps logs for email regexes; fail if any found.

fran: I can open a PR: bump sample to ^0.9.3, add `normalizeHeaders()` in http/primitive.js (runs before any lib call), unit tests for email/token/ip redaction and double-redact, and the CI logs-scan job. I'll default strict scrub to off via `REDWOOD_SCRUB_STRICT=false` and document opt-in.

ty: Also add a tiny metric `onboard.scrub.events` so we can monitor how often we redact in samples. If it spikes unexpectedly we'll investigate false positives.

sdk-bot: Related SDK changes: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/472 (ensureReqId) and https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/478 (docs + hook notes).

fran: Can we add a short quickstart note too? New users keep filing tickets: "too many debug logs" or "no request ids in logs". Something like: 
- If you see noisy DEBUG network logs, set REDWOOD_LOG_LEVEL=info for first-run.
- If you flip TELEMETRY_HOOK_ORDER, ensure SDK >=0.9.3 or enable REDWOOD_SCRUB_STRICT to avoid PII leaks.

docs: I'll add those two bullets to the Quickstart troubleshooting section once PR lands. Keep it short and prescriptive.

ty: Landing plan: (1) PR on feature branch with scrub behind flag, tests and metric, (2) CI logs-scan added to block merges if emails appear, (3) canary enable of REDWOOD_SCRUB_STRICT in onboarding CI for a few days, (4) if stable, flip default to true and update quickstart.

fran: Cool. I'll push the PR and leave my dev instance up for manual validation. Thanks :tada:

ci-bot: CI queued for branch fran/onboard-scrub: lint, unit, integration/logs-scan. :gear:

fran: Tagging support to watch for duplicate issues and docs for the quickstart blurb.
